{"sha":"1ce098a42fe93656f841130b2b093fa4d9e8c6aa","html_url":"https://github.com/AI-Riksarkivet/rask/commit/1ce098a42fe93656f841130b2b093fa4d9e8c6aa","commit":{"author":{"name":"Borg93","email":"Borg93@users.noreply.github.com","date":"2026-10-22T13:04:23Z"},"committer":{"name":"Borg93","email":"Borg93@users.noreply.github.com","date":"2026-10-22T13:04:23Z"},"message":"feat(catalog,maintenance): LH-525 — the trash is keyed by uuid, and undrop asks which one when several held the name (ADR 0173 §9)

A recoverable drop files its trash record under the object's uuid, with its namespace's uuid and, from a cascade, the
dropped namespace's uuid. A dropped name is free again at once: the refusal of a create at a trashed name goes, and with
it LH-274's 409 naming a route that answered 404. A new table's claim never takes the location the trash keeps for its
name's dropped table.

Undrop and tasks stay addressed by name. The router asks the door's rung on each trashed candidate (`?uuid=` names
one), so a door acts on, and lists, only what its caller holds a grant on. Several candidates answer the undrop 409
with each uuid and deadline; a live object of another uuid at the name, or another namespace at the name of the one
the object was dropped from, answers 409. Both undrops re-attach a table at the key its recorded URL decodes to under
the connection's root, so a registered `räksmörgås` reads again (LH-517's undrop half); the namespace undrop restores
what its own cascade filed at and under the name. The purge judges a table by its location and a namespace by its uuid,
so it reclaims a trashed table while a table created since under the name stands; tombstones and reconcile clear and
read by uuid.

Review round (Standards, Spec): fixed a table undrop into a namespace someone re-created at its parent's name, a
nested namespace undrop answering 200 over nothing, and the by-name trash read skipping a record it cannot read (it
raises now, so every holder judgement fails closed). A recoverable cascade read its root's uuid from the best-effort
event read and could answer 500; it takes the door's own identification. Parked LOWs: the unreachable trash branch in
`fga_deps._resolve`, InvalidTableStateError on the namespace door's ambiguity, a no-location table record still judged
by name at the purge, and `tasks` on a live table with a trashed predecessor asking the trashed objects' rung.

Red checks in a snapshot worktree, each on its own assertion: ambiguity (the undrop restored the first), a live holder
and a re-created parent (the undrop answered 200), the decoded key (registered cases read 404 at the double-encoded
key), the purge (refused `still registered` by the re-created name).

Bounds: the namespace half of the purge rule (a same-name namespace of another uuid) has no test; this changes a key,
so its deploy rebuilds the estate from git (ADR 0173 §12).

+"""What the undrop doors share: which trashed object an undrop restores, and where it re-attaches a table.
+
+A trash door stays addressed by name (ADR 0173 §9, [[LH-525]]). A name is free again the moment its object is
+dropped, so several trashed objects may have held one, each its own uuid with its own grants and records: an undrop
+restores exactly the one its caller names, and asks which when the name leads to several.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Any
+
+from lance_namespace import InternalError, InvalidTableStateError
+
+from service_kit.lakehouse import trash
+from service_kit.lakehouse.base_refs import decoded_segments
+
+
+def the_one_to_restore(records: list[dict[str, Any]], *, kind: str, name: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """The one trash record among ``records`` an undrop of ``name`` restores.
+
+    Raises:
+        InvalidTableStateError: Several trashed objects held the name; the answer lists each one's uuid and deadline,
+            and ``?uuid=`` names one.
+    """
+    if len(records) == 1:
+        return records[0]
+    listed = "; ".join(
+        f"{trash.object_uuid(record)} (dropped {record.get('dropped_at')}, purge-eligible after {record.get('expires_at')})" for record in records
+    )
+    raise InvalidTableStateError(f"{len(records)} dropped {kind}s held the name {name!r}: {listed}. Name the one to undrop with ?uuid=<uuid>.")
+
+
+def require_its_own_parent(record: dict[str, Any], *, standing: str | None, name: str) -> None:
+    """Refuse restoring ``record`` into a namespace other than the one it was dropped from.
+
+    A record keeps its namespace's uuid at the drop. Once that namespace is dropped too, its name is free, and another
+    namespace created there is another uuid with its own owner: restoring into it would attach the trashed object
+    under a namespace its caller was never granted a create on, while its grants still name its own.
+
+    Raises:
+        InvalidTableStateError: The live namespace at the parent's name is not the one the object was dropped from.
+    """
+    dropped_from = record.get("namespace_uuid")
+    if isinstance(dropped_from, str) and standing is not None and standing != dropped_from:
+        raise InvalidTableStateError(f"cannot undrop {name!r}: the namespace it was dropped from is gone, and another namespace holds its name now")
+
+
+def relative_location(location: str, *, root: str) -> str:
+    """The key ``location`` decodes to under ``root``: what RegisterTable takes to re-attach the table there.
+
+    The ``dir`` backend refuses an absolute location and keeps a relative one as the literal key it is given, while a
+    trash record keeps the location ``describe_table`` answered, which percent-encodes a registered table's name
+    (``…/r%C3%A4ksm%C3%B6rg%C3%A5s``). The store holds the table's bytes under the key that decodes to once
+    (``…/räksmörgås``), so that key, whole, is what the table re-attaches at ([[LH-517]]).
+
+    Raises:
+        InternalError: ``location`` names no place under ``root``, which no drop records.
+    """
+    under, base = decoded_segments(location), decoded_segments(root)
+    if under is None or base is None or len(under) <= len(base) or under[: len(base)] != base:
+        raise InternalError(f"the trashed location {location!r} names no place under its namespace root, so the table cannot be re-attached")
+    return "/".join(under[len(base) :])"}],"selection":"Only named files are saved; other changed files omitted."}
